title: Farm life, laundry deliveries and growing up in Muskogee
summary: His mother's laundry business funded his saxophone; he recalls the horse and wagon, hog killing with his grandfather, riding bareback, and Oklahoma's oil-driven growth.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Because they had the money to buy a saxophone.

Right. Yeah, because my mother was doing work, and I used to... I delivered many a bundle of laundry. We had a horse... Man, when I think of it, we was loaded! We had a horse, we had chickens, hogs... And my grandfather used to come in every Fall and help kill the hogs. And he had a smokehouse... Milt, you haven't tasted no meat yet until you taste how he smoked that meat. And he knew how to make syrup out of cane... My grandfather was... He grew the best okra. He was a farmer at heart, but he was just a vagabond! He just liked to travel from one place to another. And he was more fond, I guess, of his younger daughter, because he stayed with her more than anybody, and he was crazy about my mother because she was the oldest of them.
And that's how we got along. Because actually, my mother had them big pots where she would wash the clothes, put the clothes in there and soak it and all that...
Right. And we would deliver it, because we had a horse-and-wagon. So we delivered it...

I learned how to ride when I was a young kid. I learned how to ride bareback, almost like the Indians. And I had a horse. I could ride him out three or four miles. And boy, when that sucker he was going home, he'd take off. I'd just let him alone and just let him go, and hold on to stay on, you know. When he got back home, he slowed up. But he knew the way back home, too. I didn't have to guide him or nothin'!

And we had a... We lived a block away from the pavement. We had streetcars... Oklahoma really built up fast. I don't really know... I guess it's on account of finding oil down there. See, because when they found the oil, everybody started coming in. That's how they got all them good teachers. We had a beautiful high school and a beautiful grade school, and we had schools in all the different parts of the town. We were close to one of those forts that...
Fort Gibson. And we got to know all the Indians, because it was the beginning of the Oklahoma... At first, Oklahoma was called the Indian Territory, and then
when they made it into a state, they called it Oklahoma.
